newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Sept 5.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Sept. 5:

WASHINGTON - U.S. warplanes began patrolling an expanded "nofly" zone in southern Iraq, as Clinton declared that two days of U.S. cruise missile strikes had been a success and left Saddam Hussein "strategically worse off."
IRBIL, Iraq - Saddam's new Kurdish allies solidify control of Irbil.
EREZ CROSSING, Gaza Strip - Netanyahu shook Arafat's hand and discarded a central tenet of his Likud party career.
WASHINGTON - Top D.C. school official says system's management and finances are in state of "disarray."
WASHINGTON - D.C. education crisis was a long time coming.
WASHINGTON - Many AIDS patients find "miracle" drugs are bitter pills.

WASHINGTON - Federal judge held Susan McDougal in contempt of court after she refused to testify before Whitewater grand jury in Little Rock about whether Clinton knew about an illegal loan or purchase of a piece of property with some of loan proceeds.
